thread:
ana_finance: FYI — INV-2026-00487 for ACME (RWI-2025-AC) looks wrong. They were billed full reserved capacity for April but the dedicated pool started mid-month. Can we prorate and handle SLA credits?

maya_acct: Thanks. Onboarding date from the onboarding doc: dedicated pool activated 2026-04-11. Invoice date is 2026-04-01 (billing system charged full month).

josh_sre: Confirming — activation event in infra logs shows `2026-04-11T14:03:02Z` for the pool.

billing-bot: Invoice INV-2026-00487 generated 2026-04-01: reserved_capacity: $45,000; usage_overage: $3,200; tax: $3,576; total: $51,776. Attachment: invoice PDF (internal).

maya_acct: Quick math I ran: April has 30 days; pool active on 11th -> days charged should be 20 (11..30 inclusive = 20 days). Prorate factor = 20/30 = 0.6667. Expected reserved fee = $45,000 * 0.6667 ≈ $30,000. So prorate refund ~ $15,000 (reserved only).

kyle_sales: Also note ACME filed a support SLA incident — p99 latency breach on 2026-04-18 and 04-19. They reported ~18% SLO breach those two days. Per contract SLA table, that maps to a 1% monthly credit? need exact mapping.

maya_acct: From contract RWI-2025-AC Appendix B: 10-30% monthly breach => 1% monthly fee credit on reserved charges. For April reserved base ($45k) 1% = $450. If we apply after prorate, either we: a) apply 1% against full month $45k ($450), or b) against prorated $30k ($300). Contract language prefers applying to billed amount for the month. We should ask legal if we interpret "monthly fee" as billed amount.

ana_followup: (note: this message is from ana_finance, missent tag) Sorry ignore.

ana_finance: Proposed resolution: issue prorate refund for reserved portion ($15,000) and apply SLA credit as a negative line on April invoice. If legal insists SLA credit applies to billed amount, that's $450; if applied post-prorate it's $300. Recommend we apply $450 now to avoid dispute and note adjustment. We can net the total credit/refund against the invoice: $15,450. Apply to next invoice or process immediate refund? Thoughts? :thinking_face:

simon_ops: Approve applying a negative line to current invoice for $15,450 and also create AR adjustment ticket. We'll route refund if customer requests cash return; default is apply as credit to next invoice. :thumbsup:

maya_acct: I'll create AR ticket AR-3321 and a billing ops task to issue the negative line. GL codes: use 4305-ReservedRevenue for reversal, 5401-SLA-Credits for the SLA offset, and note external notes with contract id.

josh_sre: Can billing ops also mark the infra incident ref INC-2026-114 in the ticket so CS has traceability?

kyle_sales: I'll ping the account owner and prepare a customer note: explain prorate + SLA credit, show math, offer refund if preferred. I'll cc legal if they push the interpretation.

billing-bot: Created ticket AR-3321 and billing task TASK-8482. Assigned to maya_acct and billing-ops queue.

maya_acct: I'll push the negative line today and attach the math and infra logs. Will also include both SLA credit interpretations in the ticket (450 vs 300) and legal can confirm.

simon_ops: One more ask — tag the journal entry with period 2026-04 and include memo "Mid-quarter reserved capacity prorate + SLA credit — ACME RWI-2025-AC". Finance will post once billing ops confirms negative line.

ana_finance: Thanks everyone. I'll update the customer-facing message once billing ops confirms the credit line is posted.

kyle_sales: Great — will stand by.
